August 16, 2026 Run
Gus: Think I started having some IT band syndrome on August 6 run, about 5 miles in. Not sure of the cause. Maybe too much power output on bike without correct footwear. Then big unstable downhills definitely made it much worse (think it was improving before that). Think I need to be careful on the bike and maybe re-assess that footwear. Right lower calf and achilles started hurting a lot after second big Alps run but seem to be cooled down now - totally fine walking around and on bike yesterday. Left achilles also feeling very good too. It's really just the knee at the moment. Also been feeling the ACNES stuff on left ab side last ten days or so...not sure why. Right side (the vacuum injury) has been good.

Maybe because I contracted it a good amount during visit with Adam Weir today. On that note: / Adam think it's just a lower abdominal muscle strain. He advises staying active - continuing to run and do core exercises (core every other day), so long as pain during or next day doesn't surpass a 4 or 5. Says that it's actually good to feel a bit sore the next day; that means it was activated well, which is important for muscle repair. Titus Fierkens: Hi Gus, the Tuesday workouts are specific for 5/10k and therefore high quality with more longer T1 pace. The Sunday long runs are getting more challenging, because including serious intervalls! The focus is on staying consistent week to week, instead of increasing total mileage, I’m prioritizing higher quality. The week before your 10K will be easier so you can perform at your best. This race is currently in the plan, but add your own races (like mentioned in whatsapp ;)) because this is easier for me to see them when they’re in your schedule.
Titus Fierkens: And also more often specific hill sessions for more power, technique and speed. And if you feel good and have energy you can always do some longer WU - CD to have more milage in a week.
Titus Fierkens: So if you can please add the coming races! You're doing well, recovery and fitness is perfect so keep going 👊😊

Plan: (20:00 @ 4:59/km + 15:00 @ 4:26/km + 10:00 @ 4:06/km)
Gus: Overall felt really good. Very encouraging run. Basically no discomfort in the psoas, which I am very happy about, and felt a bit smoother at faster paces than two days ago. Only slightly concerning thing: mild discomfort in my left lower-back. I've felt this off and on for the last couple of weeks. I'm quite sure it was caused by Romanian deadlifts in the gym. I may have lifted a bit too heavy or not used proper form for a few repetitons. Will keep a close eye on this and avoid back exercises in the gym for now. Will also speak with Joost next week, so I can talk to him about it then.
Titus Fierkens: Yes, agreed, because that could give just a bit too much load, especially if the execution isn't 100% right. Let me know once you've seen Joost, what he thought of it ✅
Gus: 👍🏼👍🏼

Gus: I have a pretty old and basic GPS watch, and I think it is slow to detect new paces. I'm quite sure that my strides today were faster than shown in the data. In any case, felt pretty good today. Minimal soreness and no irritation from faster run the other day. Felt a bit awkward doing the strides today - first time running this pace in a long time - but no irritation, which I'm happy about. Psoas is a bit achy in the hours afterwards though. Will closely monitor.
Titus Fierkens: Hey Gus, doing well, and yes, especially in the first month there will still be some adjustment. Nothing to force or push, but we'll both keep an eye on that! Otherwise, trust your body and don't focus too much on the data... I filter and compare what's needed, and within 4-6 weeks I'll know exactly how to guide you on load and different training types 👊

Gus: [Dutch below] My Garmin was out of battery so I had to use Strava on my phone. This made it difficult to see the pacing for each interval, so I had to go "by feel". Still ended up close to what I wanted, though. / Felt pretty good. This was much faster than I have run in more than 16 months because Joost has had me running such slow paces for the psoas (almost never faster than 5:00/km). Injured side felt weak but not super irritated; I think it was ok. I felt my glutes working more on the injured side than usual, which was encouraging because the cornerstone of Joost's recovery program is glute strength. Curious to see what the reaction will be in next couple of days.
Gus: Oh, and sorry that this is in miles, not kilometers. I did change the settings on my Garmin but not Strava app on my phone (and as I said, I had to use Strava because my Garmin battery was dead.) In the future, I should be using the Garmin nearly 100% of the time.
